<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919340_theRebbe_24__p006">
  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions the order of the maamar, noting that the Tanya discusses toil in Torah and prayer in reverse sequence, proving the maamar's order is intentional.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And we need to understand,</t>
    <t s="1">behold, the matter of the arousal from below in Torah is seemingly primarily in the toil that must be in the study of Torah itself,</t>
    <t s="2">and the order in the maamar is that at first it explains that in order for Torah study to be proper, there must be the work and toil of prayer, and afterwards it says</t>
    <t s="3">(like an additional thing)</t>
    <t s="4">that there must be toil also in the study of Torah itself.</t>
    <t s="5">And to note,</t>
    <t s="6">that also in Tanya52</t>
    <t s="7">it speaks of these two matters,</t>
    <t s="8">toil in Torah and toil in the service of God in general, the main service being the service of prayer53,</t>
    <t s="9">and the order of matters in Tanya is that at first it brings the verse54</t>
    <t s="10">"And you shall return and see between one who serves God and one who does not serve Him,"</t>
    <t s="11">for on this verse it is stated in the Gemara that one who serves God is one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times,</t>
    <t s="12">changing the nature of habit in Torah study,</t>
    <t s="13">and this statement of our sages is the source for what is explained there that also the fulfillment of all the commandments</t>
    <t s="14">[and particularly the service of prayer]</t>
    <t s="15">must be in this manner.</t>
    <t s="16">And from this</t>
    <t s="17">(that the order of matters in the maamar is in the opposite manner from the order in Tanya)</t>
    <t s="18">it is proven even more that the order of matters in the maamar is intentional.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="16">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that since Torah is a drawing down from above to below, it does not require a multitude, unlike prayer which draws down through the work of the lower being.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing an explanation of the precision</t>
    <t s="2">(in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="3">"even though Torah is a drawing down from above to below."</t>
    <t s="4">For the explanation of this simply is,</t>
    <t s="5">that since Torah is a drawing down from above to below,</t>
    <t s="6">there is no need for a multitude.</t>
    <t s="7">For in prayer, where the drawing down is through the work of the lower being, the work of the lower being must be the work of a multitude,</t>
    <t s="8">but not so in Torah, which is a drawing down from above,</t>
    <t s="9">there is no difference whether the lower being is a multitude or an individual.</t>
    <t s="10">And according to the known55</t>
    <t s="11">that the reason that through prayer a new will is drawn down is due to the greatness of the elevation of the raising of the feminine waters,</t>
    <t s="12">"the work of Your hands You desire"56,</t>
    <t s="13">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="14">that the intention in the precision that Torah is a drawing down from above to below is also for the other side,</t>
    <t s="15">that since Torah is a drawing down from above,</t>
    <t s="16">even through the study of Torah by a multitude it is impossible to have a most elevated drawing down like the drawing down through prayer</t>
    <t s="17">[of a multitude].</t>
  </section>
  <section v="17">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the maamar prioritizes the work of prayer before Torah study because prayer effects a change in nature and draws down beyond measure, while Torah study serves as a vessel for that drawing down.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this we can explain the order of matters in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="1">that at first it explains the work and toil of prayer that must be for the sake of engaging in Torah, and afterwards the work and toil in Torah study itself,</t>
    <t s="2">for the main work and toil is the service of prayer,</t>
    <t s="3">which is therefore called "service" without qualification.</t>
    <t s="4">For the matter of service is the change of nature and habit,</t>
    <t s="5">and this is accomplished primarily through the service of prayer.</t>
    <t s="6">And particularly through the prayer of the standing [Amidah], where the person praying is like a servant before his Master57,</t>
    <t s="7">utter self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="8">Therefore the maamar precedes the work and toil of prayer that is for the sake of engaging in Torah,</t>
    <t s="9">for the work and toil of engaging in Torah</t>
    <t s="10">(in and of itself)</t>
    <t s="11">does not have the power to draw down a drawing down that is completely beyond measure relative to the work.</t>
    <t s="12">And this that through Torah study</t>
    <t s="13">(of a multitude)</t>
    <t s="14">a drawing down is made that is completely beyond measure relative to the work,</t>
    <t s="15">like the drawing down through prayer</t>
    <t s="16">(of a multitude),</t>
    <t s="17">is primarily through the work of prayer that is for the sake of engaging in Torah.</t>
    <t s="18">However, this explanation is insufficient,</t>
    <t s="19">for in Torah,</t>
    <t s="20">the drawing down that is beyond measure relative to the elevation comes in the knowledge and understanding of Torah,</t>
    <t s="21">that his success in knowledge and understanding of Torah is beyond measure relative to his toil,</t>
    <t s="22">and therefore there must also be the toil of changing nature and habit in Torah study itself,</t>
    <t s="23">for through this,</t>
    <t s="24">his study is a vessel for the drawing down that comes through the work of prayer</t>
    <t s="25">(that is for the sake of engaging in Torah).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
